H-A1.prediction: an evolved router on the htlc-limits tier sizes shards against the announced MaxHTLC and shows lower attempts than its ancestor at equal success
H-A1.observed: no evolution arm in this sweep. The standing five show the null half: on a_tight attempts move hb1 +0.17, mx_c3 +1.67, atomic1 -4.03, lnd -13.44 while success falls 8.3, 8.4, 15.8 and 10.2 points. Nobody sizes against a cap; everybody discovers it by failing.
H-A1.verdict: NOT TESTABLE BY MEASUREMENT (needs the evolution arm); the blindness it presumes is confirmed

H-A2.prediction: the champion-minus-lnd margin is SMALLER on the htlc-limits tier than on its untouched control
H-A2.observed: gap move on a_tight: hb1 +0.012 [-0.113,+0.100], mx_c3 +0.007 [-0.117,+0.103], atomic1 -0.032 [-0.137,+0.058]; on a_emp all three straddle zero too. The two champions' point estimates are POSITIVE. The arm the tight caps hurt most is lnd (-0.104 objective, -0.102 success, 9/10 files, p=.021), and the seed's margin over lnd WIDENS (+0.072, CI excludes zero).
H-A2.verdict: REFUTED. Free public bounds do not narrow the gap, which is independent support for exp-021's conclusion that the edge lives at plan time rather than in bound discovery.

H-B1.prediction: an evolved router on an inbound-fee tier carries a per-node inbound term into its edge cost and shows lower realized fee_ppm_on_success than its ancestor at equal success
H-B1.observed: no evolution arm. Standing routers: on b_heavy lnd's realized fee falls 2088 -> 320 ppm while hb1 -22, mx_c3 +62, atomic1 +185, seed -256; candidates take 7 to 39 inbound_fee_refusals per file where lnd takes zero.
H-B1.verdict: NOT TESTABLE BY MEASUREMENT; the blindness is confirmed and quantified

H-B2.prediction: inbound fees are worth more to lnd than to the champions: the champion-minus-lnd fee gap narrows and the success ordering does not change
H-B2.observed: b_heavy: lnd +0.118 objective [+0.036,+0.205], 9/1, p=.021, success +0.072, fee 2088->320 ppm. Champions flat to worse (mx_c3 -0.061*, atomic1 -0.021*, hb1 -0.036). Gap move hb1 -0.154*, mx_c3 -0.178*, atomic1 -0.139*, seed -0.119*, every CI excluding zero at p=.021, 1/9. The champions' significant lead over lnd DISAPPEARS on that tier (all three CIs now straddle zero). b_emp and mainnet as_loaded are exactly null (as_loaded: 0/0/10 ties on four routers).
H-B2.verdict: CONFIRMED, and larger than the hypothesis anticipated: the ordering does not invert but the champions lose significance. Null on both empirical rungs, so this is an authored-family result.

H-C1.prediction: a binding fee limit converts fee blindness into failures; every router's success falls and lnd's falls LEAST
H-C1.observed: hard profile 5000/4000/2000 success delta: lnd -0.020/-0.034/-0.225, seed -0.063/-0.108/-0.410, hb1 -0.200/-0.300/-0.469, mx_c3 -0.233/-0.277/-0.467, atomic1 -0.079/-0.192/-0.418. mainnet 400/100/25: lnd -0.070/-0.110/-0.160, seed -0.110/-0.180/-0.220, hb1 -0.130/-0.200/-0.240, mx_c3 -0.110/-0.190/-0.220, atomic1 -0.080/-0.140/-0.200. lnd falls least at all six rungs on both tier families.  At the full bar, the NARROWING of the champion lead is established unanimously on the mainnet family (gap move hb1 -0.154/-0.186/-0.190 at 400/100/25 ppm, 0/9/1 and 0/10/0, p=.004/.004/.002; mx_c3 -0.123/-0.174/-0.167, same shape; atomic1 -0.098 at 25 ppm, p=.004) and for hb1 at 5000 ppm on the hard profile (p=.008). The INVERSION -- lnd actually ahead -- has a CI excluding zero on c_mn_100 and c_mn_25 for hb1 and mx_c3 (-0.070 to -0.093) but a sign test of .070 to .289, so it does NOT clear the bar and is reported as a point estimate only.
H-C1.verdict: CONFIRMED, unanimously and monotonically, on both tier families. The strongest result in the sweep.

H-C2.prediction: an evolution arm on a fee-limited tier produces a router that tracks remaining budget across shards rather than one that lowers its fee weight
H-C2.observed: no evolution arm. fee_limit_failures per file grows monotonically with pressure on every candidate (seed 8.8/28.3/131.5 on hard; 346/644/707 on mainnet) and is exactly zero on lnd at all six rungs, reproducing stage C's agreement test.
H-C2.verdict: NOT TESTABLE BY MEASUREMENT; the blindness is confirmed

H-D1.prediction: an evolved router on the concurrency tier keeps a per-local-channel in-flight count and does not write a persistent bound when a first-hop failure is explained by its own reservation
H-D1.observed: no evolution arm; the claim additionally requires the mechanism to be visible in evolved source.

H-D2.prediction: the champions poison their own first hop and show rising attempts on later payments
H-D2.verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED and router-specific: the signature is hb1's (and weakly mx_c3's), atomic1 is nearly immune, and the score consequence is not significant (see H-D3).

H-D3.prediction: lnd loses less from concurrency than the champions do
H-D3.observed: knob-minus-control objective at w4: lnd -0.074*, hb1 -0.112*, mx_c3 -0.077*, atomic1 -0.029*, seed -0.067*. Champion-gap moves at w2 and w4 all straddle zero at n=20 (hb1 -0.038 [-0.107,+0.034], mx_c3 -0.003, atomic1 +0.045 [-0.008,+0.100]).
H-D3.verdict: UNDERPOWERED (pre-registered treatment for a straddling CI at n=20 on a concurrency tier). Point estimates split the champions: hb1 in the predicted direction, atomic1 in the opposite. Stage D's smoke reversal (lnd absorbing more self-contention per attempt than the seed) reproduces at w2 (0.140 vs 0.078) and washes out at w4 (0.184 vs 0.177).

E-a.prediction: latency alone is null, confirming exp-015 and exp-019
E-a.observed: on the no-traffic latency arm every one of the five routers is EXACTLY unchanged at both rungs: objective, success, attempts and fees all 0/0/10 ties, delta 0.000, lnd included. With background traffic the movements are hb1 -0.019, mx_c3 -0.015 (fast) and +0.012/+0.013 (slow), every CI straddling zero.
E-a.verdict: CONFIRMED, in the strongest form the spec allowed

E-b.prediction: latency on top of concurrency is NOT null, because latency now buys contention
E-b.observed: the mechanism is live: hb1's self-contention at w4 goes 20.9 (ctrl) / 30.7 (fast) / 56.1 (slow) per file. On score, e_w4_fast mx_c3 +0.018 and atomic1 +0.029 and e_w4_slow atomic1 +0.040 have CIs excluding zero but sign-test p of .727, .375 and .062, so none clears the pre-registered bar (CI excludes zero AND p<0.05). Direction is that latency HELPS the fastest routers under contention.
E-b.verdict: UNDERPOWERED at n=10, per the pre-registered instruction. Mechanism confirmed, score verdict not established.

E-c.prediction: under objective L the champion ordering is unchanged but the margin against lnd changes SIGN on at least one tier
E-c.observed: across seven latency tiers no margin against lnd changes sign. The champions' margins shrink on the no-traffic and sequential arms (e_na_slow hb1 +0.116 -> +0.090, mx_c3 +0.109 -> +0.088) and grow slightly for the seed and for hb1 at window 4. The champion ordering is unchanged everywhere.
E-c.verdict: REFUTED on the sign-change clause, CONFIRMED on the ordering-unchanged clause. Time-instead-of-attempts moves margins by 0.01 to 0.03, an order of magnitude short of a verdict change.

headline.question: does economic realism CLOSE the champion-vs-lnd gap, and on which mechanisms
headline.answer: On the two PRICING mechanisms (inbound fees, fee budgets) the gap narrows and the narrowing clears the pre-registered bar. On the three constraint/timing/contention mechanisms (announced htlc limits, concurrency, latency) it does not move at all.

by_stage.A_htlc_limits: NO. Gap moves straddle zero on both rungs; lnd is the arm the tight caps hurt most (-0.104, 9/10, p=.021).
by_stage.B_inbound_fees: YES on the authored heavy rung: lnd +0.118 (9/1, p=.021), every champion gap move negative with CI excluding zero (-0.139 to -0.178, 1/9, p=.021), and the champions' significant lead over lnd disappears. NULL on both empirical rungs and on the real mainnet policies (exactly zero).
by_stage.C_fee_budgets: YES, and it is the largest effect in the sweep. The narrowing clears the full bar unanimously on mainnet (hb1 -0.154/-0.186/-0.190 at 400/100/25 ppm, p=.004/.004/.002, 0/9/1 to 0/10/0; mx_c3 -0.123/-0.174/-0.167; atomic1 -0.098 at 25 ppm) and for hb1 at 5000 ppm on the hard profile. The champions' lead over lnd goes from +0.097* on the clean mainnet tier to a NEGATIVE point estimate at every rung (hb1 -0.057/-0.089/-0.093, mx_c3 -0.026/-0.077/-0.070) with CIs excluding zero at 100 and 25 ppm but sign tests of .07 to .29, so the inversion itself is not established at the bar. atomic1 is the exception, holding +0.061 at 400 ppm and a tie at 25 ppm: the fee-pressure-robust champion.
by_stage.D_concurrency: NO. Concurrency significantly costs EVERY router at window 4 (knob minus control clears the full bar: lnd -0.074 p<.001, hb1 -0.112 p=.021, mx_c3 -0.077 p=.004, atomic1 -0.029 p=.031) but it costs them about equally: every champion-gap move straddles zero at n=20. Reported as UNDERPOWERED per the pre-registered rule, not as a null.
by_stage.E_latency: NO. E-a exactly null, E-b not established, objective L never flips a sign.

headline.reading: The champions' edge is informational, not a pricing edge. Where the differentiator is a calibrated weight function over fees, inbound fees and budgets, lnd wins the ground back, up to and including a significant inversion on mainnet under fee pressure. Where the differentiator is knowledge of hidden liquidity (announced caps, contention, timing), the gap is untouched. That is the pre-registered 'economic realism could close the champion gap' outcome, arriving with a sharp mechanism attribution: port the belief system, not the cost model.

verdict_bar: a directional claim requires the bootstrap CI to exclude zero AND the two-sided sign test to reach p<0.05 (design spec, verdict criterion 4). Cells clearing only the CI are reported as such.
